```{r}
#| label: setup
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(knitr)

# Read the 2026 election precinct data
results <- read_csv("results_pct_20261103.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Voting Method by Party

This section examines how Democrats and Republicans cast their ballots in the statewide US Senate race (Early Voting, Election Day, or Absentee by Mail).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-methods
#| tbl-cap: "Voting Method Breakdown by Party (US Senate)"

# Summarize vote counts by party and voting method
methods_summary <- results |>
  filter(`Contest Name` == "US SENATE", `Choice Party` %in% c("DEM", "REP")) |>
  summarize(
    `Early Voting` = sum(`Early Voting`, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Election Day` = sum(`Election Day`, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Absentee by Mail` = sum(`Absentee by Mail`, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = `Choice Party`
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(`Early Voting`, `Election Day`, `Absentee by Mail`),
    names_to = "Method",
    values_to = "Votes"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Percentage = Votes / sum(Votes),
    .by = `Choice Party`
  )

# Display summary table
methods_summary |>
  mutate(
    `Total Votes` = comma(Votes),
    Share = percent(Percentage, accuracy = 0.1)
  ) |>
  select(`Party` = `Choice Party`, `Voting Method` = Method, `Total Votes`, Share) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-methods
#| fig-cap: "Comparison of Voting Methods by Party in the 2026 US Senate Race"

# Plot the percentage of votes cast via each method
ggplot(methods_summary, aes(x = Method, y = Percentage, fill = `Choice Party`)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("DEM" = "#2166ac", "REP" = "#b2182b"),
    labels = c("DEM" = "Democrat", "REP" = "Republican")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Voting Method by Party in North Carolina",
    subtitle = "2026 US Senate Race",
    x = "Voting Method",
    y = "Share of Party's Total Votes",
    fill = "Party"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## County Voting Trends Map

The map below illustrates party vote margins across all 100 North Carolina counties for the US Senate race. Blue indicates a Democratic margin, and red indicates a Republican margin.

```{r}
#| label: fig-map
#| fig-cap: "County Vote Margins in the 2026 North Carolina US Senate Race"

# Compute Democratic vs. Republican margin by county
county_margin <- results |>
  filter(`Contest Name` == "US SENATE", `Choice Party` %in% c("DEM", "REP")) |>
  summarize(votes = sum(`Total Votes`, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(County, `Choice Party`)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = `Choice Party`, values_from = votes, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(
    subregion = tolower(County),
    dem_margin = (DEM - REP) / (DEM + REP)
  )

# Merge with North Carolina county map coordinates
nc_map <- map_data("county", "north carolina") |>
  left_join(county_margin, by = "subregion")

# Draw choropleth map
ggplot(nc_map, aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group, fill = dem_margin)) +
  geom_polygon(color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  coord_quickmap() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#b2182b",
    mid = "#f7f7f7",
    high = "#2166ac",
    midpoint = 0,
    labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    name = "Margin (DEM vs REP)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "2026 North Carolina US Senate Results by County",
    subtitle = "Margin: (DEM - REP) / (DEM + REP)"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )
```

::: {.callout-note}
### How to Read This Map

- **Blue:** Counties won by the Democratic candidate (higher percentages indicate larger victory margins, commonly in urban centers like Wake, Durham, and Mecklenburg).
- **Red:** Counties won by the Republican candidate (strongest across rural counties).
- **White / Light Shading:** Close or competitive counties where vote shares were nearly even.
:::

## Party Affiliation by Age Group

This section looks at voter registration statistics across North Carolina to compare how party affiliations (Democrat, Republican, and Unaffiliated) vary across age cohorts.

```{r}
#| label: fig-age-party
#| fig-cap: "Registered Voters by Age Group and Party Affiliation (November 2026)"

# Read voter registration statistics
voter_stats <- read_tsv("voter_stats_20261103.zip", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Filter and summarize party affiliation across age groups
age_party <- voter_stats |>
  filter(
    party_cd %in% c("DEM", "REP", "UNA"),
    age %in% c("Age 18 - 25", "Age 26 - 40", "Age 41 - 65", "Age Over 66")
  ) |>
  summarize(total_voters = sum(total_voters, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(party_cd, age)) |>
  mutate(
    age = factor(age, levels = c("Age 18 - 25", "Age 26 - 40", "Age 41 - 65", "Age Over 66")),
    party = factor(party_cd, levels = c("DEM", "UNA", "REP"), labels = c("Democrat", "Unaffiliated", "Republican")),
    share = total_voters / sum(total_voters),
    label = percent(share, accuracy = 0.1),
    .by = age
  )

# Bar plot comparing age distribution across parties with percentages
ggplot(age_party, aes(x = age, y = share, fill = party)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = label),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    vjust = -0.4,
    size = 3.2
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, 0.62)) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Democrat" = "#2166ac", "Unaffiliated" = "#8073ac", "Republican" = "#b2182b")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Registered Voters by Age and Party in North Carolina",
    subtitle = "Percentage breakdown within each age cohort",
    x = "Age Group",
    y = "Share of Age Group",
    fill = "Party Affiliation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```
